filename: Variability in the Global Ocean Carbon Sink From 1959 to 2020 by Correcting Models With Observations - Bennington - 2022 - Geophysical Research Letters - Wiley Online Library.pdf
title: Variability in the Global Ocean Carbon Sink From 1959 to 2020 by Correcting Models With Observations
code_availability: Project code (Python) freely available on Github to prepare observational data for the machine learning algorithm, utilize XGBoost, and analyze the resulting reconstructed misfits: https://github.com/valbennington/LDEO_HPD_extension
testbed_rationale: This paper produces an observation/model-derived gridded surface ocean pCO2 and flux data product (reconstruction/gap-filling) rather than training data or testbeds for subgrid physical parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Extreme data sparsity of pCO2 observations prior to the 1980s prevents purely data-driven machine learning reconstructions.
Chlorophyll-a satellite observations do not start until 1998, requiring climatologies prior to that.
Observational coverage is especially sparse in regions like the Indian Ocean and Southern Ocean, increasing uncertainty.
Pre-1982 data like GEOSECS TA and DIC have documented inaccuracies and were excluded from modern syntheses (GLODAP).
extraction_notes: The study extends LDEO-HPD backwards from 1982 to 1959 by using the 2000-2020 climatological mean model-data misfit learned via XGBoost to bias-correct 8 ocean biogeochemical models (GOBMs). The research acknowledges support from NSF LEAP STC (Award 2019625).
